The moment I spot one, my heart races, my hands get clammy, and I can’t think about anything else. I’ll be in the middle of writing a paragraph, and a single bird outside the window ruins everything. My wife says it’s irrational, and I know it sounds strange for a grown man to fear pigeons, but the fear feels real.

I don’t worry much about my health, finances, or even my children—they’re grown and doing fine. Honestly, outside of birds, I’m fairly easygoing. But when it comes to pigeons—on rooftops, in parks, flying past the window—I can’t focus on anything else. I avoid walking outside in the mornings because that’s when they gather. It’s only birds. Nothing else triggers this. I can be in a crowded room with no issue, but a single feather on the sidewalk sets me off.
